items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.

items._cn_summary: 这是一张由瑞典小提琴家 Mats Edén 与两位挪威音乐家组成的室内乐风格民谣专辑，演绎斯堪的纳维亚传统舞曲。三位音乐家均长期致力于打破音乐类型边界——Tellef Kvifte 曾是挪威跨界乐队 Slinkombas 成员，常以竖笛、萨克斯、风笛等跨文化乐器演奏；其子 Knut Kvifte Nesheim 则以鼓手与作曲家身份模糊流派界限。专辑以挪威 Setesdal 山谷的小提琴曲《Fossgrimen》开篇，借水妖传说暗示北欧舞曲表面欢愉下暗藏的复杂情绪。整体演奏接近室内乐语境，强调三位乐手之间的音乐对话与素材深层含义的探索，而非舞蹈伴奏功能。编排上呈现即兴碎片化与即兴延展的特质，传统旋律在解构与重组中显露出实验色彩，是传统与现代交融的一次细腻尝试。

items.body: Sendas by Omar Sosa True to a Monk-inspired commitment never to play the same thing twice, Cuban pianist and composer Omar Sosa�s Sendas (Pathways), his latest solo offering, is the vivid invention of a pensive, restlessly creative, evolutionary artistry. As with all Sosa�s work, Sendas is the fortunate product of serendipity. In 2021 the COVID lockdown was underway, his marriage was ending, and a scheduled Milan appearance cancellation garnered an invitation to record at the Fazioli Pianoforti Concert Hall, annex to the renowned Italian piano manufactory in Sacile, Pordenone, about an hour northeast of Venice. At Fazioli, Sosa found himself in august company. Herbie Hancock and a host of classical pianists are Fazioli artists. Among the institutions that have embraced the Fazioli sound are the Juilliard School, Teatro La Fenice (Venice), the Budapest Palace of Arts, the Paris Conservatory, the Beijing Grand Theatre, and the universities of Salzburg, Graz, and Vienna. An unscripted two-hour solo improvisation on a Fazioli grand in the empty concert hall provided the raw audio for Sendas , later to be flavored in the mix, sparsely, with voice clips, percussion, loops, field recordings, found sounds effects that Sosa has collected over a career spanning four decades. As Sosa related to me soon after completing the post-production of Sendas , �Humanity is spiritually lost. We humans are all in this together. We need to evolve, but always keeping the traditions, walking with a strong, determined pace. We need more grounded music with overtones that resonate with the lower chakras� like throat singing, a mantra of the universal music.� �Creativity is about combining all your influences in a new way. I don�t aspire to be jazz, Latin, timba, reggaeton, classical. I avoid styles, but I respect the forms.� �I try not to think about how listeners will receive it but I do try to address their expectations, and go with the music to some other new place. Many free spirits come to listen, to be a part of the journey we are on.� Sosa laughs, �My son says, �Your niche is really small.� But the people who come really are there to be part of what we are going to do.� �Economics, technology, the streaming ear wash, algorithms all want to put you into a defined category � and so do many music journalists! The industry�s mentality is that any investment in artists must be defined by market categories to be profitable.� �But I play to be free of that,� Sosa says. �I play without thinking. There are no wrong notes. I love the first take. That�s the take, the natural voice of your soul. �Less is more� is a mantra in my life and music.� Consider the opening of �Inside the Spirit,� easing in leisurely, reaching over the keyboard into the resonant heart of the instrument, plucking and stroking the strings, teasing out a fuller resonance � only later to be embellished in the studio mix with light percussion and the muted Spanish-language refrain of a pregonero or street vendor, as might be heard in the calles of Havana or any other Latin American barrio. Sendas by Omar Sosa Moving from the secular to the sacred, �Deities Serenade� is an Afro-Cuban invocation of the shape-shifting divine, yet with ample room for ecumenical recasting in accord with a listener�s own self-location. �Inside My Soul� and �Something from Home� are Sosa works that to my ear may be an intuitive response to the distant call of Chopin�s "Nocturnes," to which Sosa says he listened every night for two years as a conservatory student in Cuba. Sendas by Omar Sosa �Caribbean Movement� and �Shirma� speak to Sosa�s rootedness in the lyrical, rhythmic, and harmonic heritage of the plantation islands where African and European cultures tragically entwined. In the violent forging of the world�s first truly modern people, social, cultural, linguistic, and musical displacements proved more flexible and accommodating than many of those same people, who shaped a contentious convergence of traditions into a changing same that persists into the unfolding present, ever yet to come. With expressive transcendence such as this, seeking to reduce the spiritual essence and inspiration of Sosa�s music to words is rather a fool�s errand. Better rather to listen, to contemplate, to perceive the pathway, to wander the sonic sendas coursing to the next way station without prejudice or preconception. To that end, Scott Price, Sosa�s longtime manager and friend relates, �We are using Sendas as the springboard for our first experiments in AI-generated Omar Sosa music videos.� Absent the opportunity to see and hear Sosa perform live, the palpable ideal, these ancillary audiovisual experiments further the ineffability of his artistic quest, the unique nature of the listening experience and all that ensues.

items._cn_summary: 古巴钢琴家 Omar Sosa 在意大利 Fazioli 钢琴厅完成了一场两小时无脚本独奏即兴录音，成为这张专辑的原始素材。录制期间他身处新冠封锁与个人生活变动的交汇点，作品呈现出沉思而不断演变的创作状态。后期制作中，他以稀疏的方式叠加人声采样、打击乐、循环音、田野录音与拾得声响，为即兴钢琴增添层次与空间感。Sosa 明确拒绝被归入爵士、拉丁或古典等任何风格范畴，强调'没有错误的音符'与'少即是多'的美学，追求第一遍录音的自然性。专辑开篇曲展示了直接伸入琴弦内部以拨弄、抚摸激发更丰富共鸣的演奏方式，融合了极简触感与实验声响探索。

items.body: Photo: Aboubacar Traor� A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The newly released album from Malian musicians Neba Solo and Benego Diakit� is the outcome of a project which began in 2013 when Solo and Diakit�, playing balafon and n'goni respectively, were recorded by Bamako producer Ousmane Ha�dara. He played the result to another record producer, Nick Gold, who was completely taken by what he heard and together they decided to work on the recording to produce a finished album, also enlisting English musician Sonny Johns to help with the production. Gold had previously brought together Ali Farka Tour� and Toumani Diabat� to record what was to become the very successful album In the Heart of the Moon and this was a similar story, Solo and Diakit� also being established Malian musicians coming from different musical backgrounds. Indeed, the balafon and n'goni, though both widely associated with Malian music, are seldom played together. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking , released as a double CD, is very much an album of two halves. The recordings made in 2013 of the two musicians playing together were transformed over time into ensemble arrangements with the addition of other musicians playing strings, mellotron, guitar and percussion, plus overdubbed vocals from Solo and three female singers. These reworked tracks make up the first half of the album. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The opening track, �Djin� Mogo Tiki� begins with a capella backing vocals before Diakit� introduces a repeated riff on the n'goni over which Solo improvises on the balafon while also taking the lead vocal, a pattern which forms the basis of all the tracks, with the augmented instrumentation creating further layers of interest. �Djin� Mogo Tiki� is one of two tracks to have strings added and these sit well, used sparingly to provide short rhythmic motifs, thankfully belying any fears that might be raised by mention of a string arrangement. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The reinvention of these pieces, clearly done with the co-operation of both Solo and Diakit�, may be radical but it has nevertheless been carried out with consideration and musical sensibility. �Yeredon Bali� begins with a few phrases from Solo's balafon, to be joined by Diakit�'s n'goni, some light percussion and hand claps and then more of the female backing vocals, supporting Solo's vocal in the call and response style characteristic of so much Mande music. In this case the vocal content is the only significant addition to the original duo recording, but significant it is because, in the nature of things, once a vocal line is added that becomes the main focus of attention. What makes the format of this album particularly intriguing is that the final six tracks give us the opportunity of hearing the original, unadorned versions of most of the arranged tracks as first recorded by Neba Solo and Benego Diakit�. They are referred to as the �Garden Demos� since they were recorded in a Bamako garden under a mango tree. Without the added vocals the focus shifts to the interplay between the two musicians, and the meaning of the music changes. "Djine Mogo Tiki (Garden Demo excerpt) For example, we are offered two versions of "Djin� Mogo Tiki," first appearing as the album's opening track in its arranged version, then later in the original duo take. Perhaps this has been done to show two sides of the same story, with an awareness too of differences in what audiences are looking for. The arranged tracks, with their instrumental variety and vocal additions, certainly work well and might help give the music wider appeal. But if you are someone who is captivated by listening to fine players engaged in a musical conversation, eavesdropping on the almost telepathic interaction taking place as the two musicians explore the common ground between them, then it's really already there in the earlier Garden Demos, the final six tracks of A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking .

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由马里音乐家Neba Solo与Benego Diakité合作，将巴拉风琴与恩戈尼两种马里传统乐器的对话作为核心框架。2013年的原始二重奏录音由Bamako制作人Ousmane Haïdara录制，后经Nick Gold与Sonny Johns参与后期制作，扩展为加入弦乐、mellotron、吉他与打击乐的合奏编曲，并叠加了Solo的人声与三位女歌手的和声。专辑以双CD形式呈现，第一部分是经过重新编排的扩展版本，第二部分保留了原始录音的亲密感。音乐结构以反复的恩戈尼riff为底，巴拉风琴即兴在上方展开，呼应马里音乐中典型的call-and-response人声传统。制作人对原始素材的再创造具有相当的克制感，弦乐编排使用节制，仅作为短促的节奏点缀出现，避免了过度甜腻。

items.body:
Photo: Claudia de Ventura
Crete�s Stelios Petrakis is at the peak of players of his island�s best-known traditional instrument, the Cretan lyra, a small pear-shaped fiddle held vertically on the knee. Its three bowed strings are stopped by the fingernails of the non-bowing hand rather than being pressed to the fingerboard. Its sound hovers on the enticing edge between fundamental and harmonics.
Petrakis is also a leading luthier, making the lyras and the other instruments he plays, including the traditional metal-strung lute laouto, and in conjunction with Ross Daly he�s developed and plays a range of lyras with ringing sympathetic strings.
True to its title, this an album of his lyra, and laouto, with a panoply of other traditional instruments played by musicians of equal stature to Petrakis, in music of rich lyricism, in melody and texture.
�Astro Sti Gaza� (�Star in Gaza�), a wish for peace written by Petrakis with lyrics by his brother Yannis Petrakis, opens the album. At first a string drone, then Petrakis�s laouto and lyra, Ma�lle Duchemin�s harp, Pavlos Spyropoulos�s double bass, and the percussion of Iranian Bijan Chemirani, who plays frame and flask hand-drums on most tracks. The dark, sinuous instrumental line is tracked by the husky vocal of Giorgis Xylouris, who sings on three tracks, the other six being instrumental. �Nathenas,� a traditional Cretan song in asymmetric rhythms, has a powerful ensemble of lyra, laouto, frame-drum, stick-hit davul, topped out by Breton Sylvain Barou�s reeds and Armenian shvi whistle.
�Anglianico,� a stately melody composed by Petrakis, has the tremolo mandolins of Valencian musician Efr�n L�pez and Michalis Kontaxakis in an elegant almost orchestral sound with lyra, guitars (Antonis Voumvoulakis and Samuel Mele), Spyropoulos�s double bass, and the accordion of Mattia Marco Gregoriadis on whose improvisation the tarantella-like �Pukan� is based.
Chemirani is particularly featured on his composition �Panj Pol,� a short finger-rippling, slapping solo on zarb flask-drum whose rhythm is the foundation for the song that it breaks into, �Agrilos,� by Petrakis with lyrics by brother Yannis celebrating the wine-producing district of Crete where they grew up. It develops into a big sound of massed instruments, with a break on frame-drum and Sakir Oran Uygan�s big double-headed davul drum before a surge of squealing tulum bagpipe and other wind instruments from Barou.
�Evlerin �n� Mersin,� a traditional tune from Asia Minor, has a march-like feel, beginning with keening lyra over a slow, inexorable drum pulse, building to soaring epic as more instruments join, peaking with Barou�s zurnas. �Muixeranga,� again with a steady, imposing pulse, is an anthemic tune played in Valencia during the Muixeranga, the traditional building of excitingly high pyramidal human towers in which the big and strong form the bottom layers and the youngest and lightest clamber up to form the topmost. Petrakis intends the track as a message of support to Valencia following the climate-change-driven floods of 2024.
Preluded and accompanied by ringing 3/4 time arpeggiating plucked strings and percussion, with the melody played on lyra, the source of �Nothing Else Matters,� is unexpected: it�s a beautiful version, evocative of memory and perhaps sadness, of a Metallica number.

items._cn_summary: 克里特岛里拉琴演奏家兼制琴师 Stelios Petrakis 的专辑，以里拉琴和拉乌托琴为核心，邀请来自希腊、布列塔尼、亚美尼亚、瓦伦西亚、伊朗等地不同传统的器乐演奏家共同录制。专辑融合东地中海、北非、高加索及伊比利亚传统乐器与演奏语汇，作品包含传统曲调与原创器乐曲，织体丰富，强调旋律线条与即兴层次。专辑开篇《Astro Sti Gaza》以弦乐持续音与人声展开，带有和平祈愿主题；其他曲目涵盖非对称节奏的克里特民歌、塔兰泰拉式即兴及人塔仪式主题的进行曲风格段落。乐评详细描述了各曲目的乐器配置、编曲结构与文化背景，体现出跨地中海传统音乐的深度交融。

items.body: sMiLes by Jowee Omicil B orn in Montreal, Haitian-Canadian musician-composer Jowee Omicil plays a fabulous variety of saxophones, clarinets, trumpets, flutes, piano, and keyboards. He came of age in the choral milieu of his father�s Montreal congregation, studied saxophone and music education at Berklee, and gleaned much from engagement with figures including Wyclef Jean, Tony Allen, Ibrahim Maalouf, Roy Hargrove, Kenny Garrett, Pharoah Sanders, Branford Marsalis, and Marcus Miller among others. Over the course of 2025, Omicil released sMiLes one song per month, each accompanied by a philosophizing podcast. The album opens with a striking reinterpretation of singer and Civil Rights activist Abbey Lincoln�s �Throw It Away,� whose message Omicil invokes in his voiceover, an expression of kinship in creative philosophical outlook. (For good measure, Omicil revisits the title on a distinctive �Throw it Away - FuLL oF LoVe Remix.�) Lincoln�s own 2007 rendition on Abbey Sings (Verve) offers critical context, itself worth a comparative audition for the original melody and the contemplative character of her lyrics. Throw it away, throw it away Give your love, live your life, each and every day And keep your hand wide open, let the sun shine through, Because you can never lose a thing, if it belongs to you. In less accomplished hands, the quirky sampling, effects, instrumentation, and wide-ranging, scruffy, sonic bricolage of sMiLes could make for one muddy m�lange. But no danger lies here in Jowee�s paradoxical, provocative, sound-shifting extended groove. Omicil's voice and sax blend almost imperceptibly in �SOeuR FeLiX AKA BeeHive.� In �Trip to GHanA,� polyrhythm meets wah-tone high-life guitar, cackly sax, and wordless vocalise. sMiLes by Jowee Omicil sMiLes by Jowee Omicil Feat. Mawuena Kodjovi Other titles transport the listener to Haiti, Morocco, Cape Verde, Jupiter, and Mali. �LeTTre Du MALi PouR JonaTHan� is a meditative, revelatory piano solo nearly ten minutes in length. sMiLes by Jowee Omicil sMiLes may invoke the free-blowing spirit of Miles (as on the sound-effected �MiLes ConvoY�), but there is no anxiety of influence here. Far from a rote genuflection to musical antecedents, the prevailing voice throughout is purely Omicil�s. As he counsels, �trust the note.� "Seek for the sound that is within you and the [instrument] will drive you to your destination� the singularity of sound is what I have always been searching for, the sound that comes from the heart, the sound that maybe, perhaps, is only heard in nature, this is what we are looking for when we are talking about sound� deep down, heartfelt uniqueness, always connected with the spirits�" - Jowee Omicil In accord with his music education formation, Omicil also leads music workshops through his BasH! AkademY, �a close-knit setting embracing spontaneity, authenticity, and shared growth,� which in 2025 included �a nomadic music experience traveling the world� to Mindelo, Cabo Verde. In 2026 Omicil will perform in New York, Canada, Martinique, France, Germany, Austria, Poland, Romania, the UK, and an African tour in the planning stage.

items._cn_summary: 海地裔加拿大音乐家Jowee Omicil的专辑以每月一首的形式在2025年发行，融合萨克斯、单簧管、钢琴与电子采样等元素，呈现出跨越海地、摩洛哥、佛得角、加纳、马里等地的全球音乐视野。专辑以Abbey Lincoln民权作品的重新诠释开篇，展现对前辈精神的承继。制作中大量使用拼贴式采样、音效处理与多元节奏（复合节奏与高life吉他并置），将自由即兴的吹奏精神与Miles Davis式的探索意识融入一首近十分钟的沉思钢琴独奏。Omicil的声音与萨克斯在某些曲目中几乎不可分割地交织，体现出对声音本源的追求——来自内心、与自然相连的声音。该专辑在实验拼贴与可听性之间找到平衡，展现了跨文化融合的独特视角。

items.body: Review by sgtpepper — Pat Metheny Group did benefit from a 4-year release break. The previous "First Circle" album was a step into a new territory (world music, rock with some pop accessibility) and a step away from the jazz territory.The good news is that the band, in the same line-up, blends the best of the both worlds to produce a lyrical, soothing yet sophisticated fusion. The rhythm elements are emphasized by busy yet sensitive drumming such as on the first Latin-friendly "Minuano". Mays lays some great moods with piano soloing or synth chords. The music flows steadily yet doesn't run hastily and goes hand in hand with painting pictures and atmosphere. The famous and slightly melancholic "Last train home" has indeed similarities to a driving train with signals. "It's just the talk" belongs to the best PMG tracks from the Brazilian arsenal with the band firing on all cylinders.Singing without words and mainly as an instrument was an excellent idea.Towards the end of the album, we get to hear a curious solo synth reflection, followed by a melancholic accessible keyboard-guitar duet.This is an excellent PMG album, in fact one of their best!
items._genre: jazz fusion / world music / contemporary jazz
items._cn_summary: Pat Metheny Group 经过四年沉淀后推出的这张专辑，将世界音乐元素与爵士融合的抒情性巧妙结合。乐队在保留原有编制的基础上，融入了拉丁节奏与巴西音乐色彩，键盘与吉他之间的对谈构筑出如绘画般的氛围感。'Minuano' 展现了拉丁化的律动处理，'Last Train Home' 以忧郁的旋律模拟列车行进意象，而 'It's Just the Talk' 则展现了乐队在巴西素材上的最佳状态。专辑中器乐化的'歌唱'概念颇具新意——人声作为乐器融入编曲而非主导旋律，使得音乐在流畅行进中维持了器乐融合的高度。整体而言，这是一张平衡了可听性与艺术性的成熟作品，但偏向柔和流畅的抒情表达，在实验性层面着墨有限。

The inclusion of Pedro Aznar underlines the world music touches and brings different emotions than just lyricism or introspection, which were apparent on the previous ou
items.body: Review by sgtpepper — For fans of the early Pat Metheny Group, the first album with the new drummer, Paul Wertico, could be quite a surprise. Drumming is more rock-oriented, louder but certainly not simple. Behind the normal jazz-fusion explorations, there are hints of more streamlined approach with more focus on melodies. The inclusion of Pedro Aznar underlines the world music touches and brings different emotions than just lyricism or introspection, which were apparent on the previous outputs. Aznar vocal fits well into the more accessible music frame.This slightly experimental album should appeal to the majority of PMG fans; however fusion purists may not find enough entertainment in its 49 minutes of length.
items._genre: jazz fusion / world music / jazz rock
items._cn_summary: 这是Pat Metheny Group迎来新鼓手Paul Wertico后的首张专辑，鼓点风格更偏向摇滚化，力度更强且节奏复杂。整体在常规爵士融合探索之外，融入了更多旋律导向的精简编排。南美音乐人Pedro Aznar的加入为作品增添了世界音乐色彩，其人声与器乐交织，呈现出不同于前作抒情内省的气质。专辑具有一定的实验性尝试，音乐框架更为亲和可及，但深度融合爵士纯正派听众可能认为娱乐性不足。全长约49分钟，融合了爵士摇滚与世界音乐元素，是PMG系列中风格转折的一张作品。

items.body: Tara Clerkin Trio Somewhere Good Somewhere Good is a beautifully patient listen that shows Tara Clerkin Trio refining their delicate chamber-inflected sound Somewhere Good by Tara Clerkin Trio Arriving after a steady run of cult-leaning releases on World of Echo, Tara Clerkin Trio’s Somewhere Good finds the Bristol-based collective refining a language they’ve been sketching since their 2020 debut. Following the quietly celebrated EPs In Spring and On The Turning Ground, this first full-length feels like an expansion of their hazy, chamber-like palette into something more deliberately panoramic, yet resistant to easy categorisation. In a contemporary landscape that often flattens “experimental” music into genre tags, the trio continue to operate in a space where trip-hop echoes, folk intimacies and modern classical restraint all drift... The post Tara Clerkin Trio – Somewhere Good appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是布里斯托乐队的首张全长作品，延续了他们自2020年首张EP以来对内敛音色的探索。乐评指出他们在trip-hop回响、民谣私密感与现代古典克制之间找到了交汇点，形成一种雾气弥漫的室内乐质感。整张专辑的聆听体验被形容为耐心而细腻，拒绝被简单的风格标签归类。在当代乐坛倾向于将实验音乐扁平化为流派标签的环境下，他们坚持在多元素之间自由漂浮的创作方式本身就是一种立场。制作呈现出一种刻意拉宽的全景感，同时保持私密气息。

items.body: Gastr del Sol8 languagesFrom Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia(Redirected from Gastr Del Sol)Gastr del SolOriginChicago, Illinois, United StatesGenresPost-rockavant-gardeYears active1991-1998LabelsTeenbeat, Drag City, Table of the ElementsPast membersDavid GrubbsJim O'RourkeBundy K. BrownJohn McEntireGastr del Sol was an American band, consisting for most of their career of David Grubbs and Jim O'Rourke, based in Chicago.[1] Between 1993 and 1998, they released four albums and three EPs.Biography[edit]Grubbs formed the band in 1991 from the line-up of the group Bastro, with Bundy K. Brown and John McEntire on bass guitar and drums respectively.[1] The group had previously premiered sketches of songs in their final shows, with the live recordings being released in 2005 as Antlers, which demonstrated their departure from post-hardcore to focus on unconventional math rock. With their new name being derived from a combination of their previous name, and the name of a race horse (Gato del Sol),[2] the trio released their first album, The Serpentine Similar in 1993, with several songs working off of Grubbs' sketches. Brown and McEntire left to join Tortoise the following year, and guitarist/composer/producer Jim O'Rourke joined.[1] The group became mainly a collaboration between Grubbs and O'Rourke, joined by an ever-changing collection of guests.[1] Though McEntire was no longer a full member, he continued contributing to many Gastr del Sol recordings and concerts.Most releases by this line-up were on Chicago's Drag City, beginning with the acoustic guitar-based Crookt, Crackt, or Fly in 1994.[1] "Work From Smoke", the centerpiece of this album which evolved from another live Bastro sketch, fused Grubbs and O'Rourke's penchant for atonal guitar interplay with bass clarinet and Grubbs's increasingly surrealist lyrics. Sam Prekop named the band The Sea and Cake after a misreading of the album's song "The C in Cake". A pair of releases followed quickly in 1995. The Mirror Repair EP added elements of electroacoustic music. The Harp Factory on Lake Street, released on the Table of the Elements label, was their most experimental work, a piece for chamber orchestra with only occasional voice and piano from Grubbs.[1] Also in 1995, the band contributed the song "Quietly Approaching" to the AIDS benefit album Red Hot + Bothered produced by the Red Hot Organization.Upgrade & Afterlife, released in 1996, included contributions from experimental musicians Kevin Drumm, Günter Müller and Tony Conrad.[1] Meanwhile, with the release of Camoufleur in 1998, Gastr del Sol progressed further into conventional melodicism with the resulting album being described by critics as chamber pop, creating their most accessible and popular album.[1] Its chord patterns, melodies, and flugelhorn and string-heavy arrangements prefigured O'Rourke's later releases such as Eureka. The album was co-written with Markus Popp, of the pioneering German glitch group Oval, who contributed the electronic aspects of the album.[1] Both albums also featured drum and percussion contributions from McEntire. After Camoufleur, due to personal differences and grievances, the duo split up. Grubbs and O'Rourke have both continued to release albums under their own names in the fields of rock, pop, and experimental music.[1]In 2024, Drag City released We Have Dozens of Titles, a 3LP/2CD retrospective boxset containing various rare or unreleased studio and live recordings made by the band between 1993 and 1998.Discography[edit]The Serpentine Similar (Teenbeat/Drag City, 1993)Twenty Songs Less (Teenbeat, 1993)Crookt, Crackt, or Fly (Drag City, 1994)Mirror Repair EP (Drag City, 1994)The Harp Factory on Lake Street (Table of the Elements, 1995)The Japanese Room at LA Pagode (with Tony Conrad) (Table of the Elements, 1995)Upgrade & Afterlife (Drag City, 1996)Camoufleur (Drag City, 1998)[1]We Have Dozens of Titles (Drag City, 2024)References[edit]^ Jump up to:a b c d e f g h i j k Colin Larkin, ed. (2000). The Virgin Encyclopedia of Nineties Music (First ed.). Virgin Books. p. 170. ISBN 0-7535-0427-8.^ "Grubbs Interview 1998". Paristransatlantic.com. June 28, 1998. items._cn_summary: Gastr del Sol是来自芝加哥的实验乐队，活跃于1991至1998年间。早期三人阵容脱胎于post-hardcore团体Bastro，逐渐转向非传统的math rock路线。1994年Jim O'Rourke加入后，乐队核心变为David Grubbs与O'Rourke的合作，大量使用原声吉他、无调性吉他对话、低音单簧管以及超现实主义歌词，并融入电声音乐元素。1995年的《The Harp Factory on Lake Street》由室内管弦乐团演奏，辅以偶尔的人声与钢琴，是最具实验性的一张作品。1998年的《Camoufleur》则进一步回归旋律性。乐队在Drag City等独立厂牌发行作品，与Tortoise等芝加哥实验圈关系密切。整体而言，这是一支持续探索后摇滚与前卫音乐边界的乐队，适合对非传统吉他音乐和实验结构感兴趣的听众。

items._cn_summary: 本文并非传统乐评，而是对John Cale《New York In The 1960s》三碟套装再版的唱片信息罗列。套装收录三张专辑：《Sun Blindness Music》以Vox Continental电风琴为主，长达四十三分钟的持续音块展现极简嗡鸣美学；《Dream Interpretation》与《Stainless Gamelan》收录与Tony Conrad、Angus MacLise、Sterling Morrison、Terry Jennings等六十年代纽约地下场景核心人物的室内乐即兴，涵盖中提琴、小提琴、钢片琴琴、磁带循环与嘶吼人声；此外附赠Jack Smith两首地下电影配乐。整体呈现出剧场艺术、磁带音乐、噪音实验与原音乐器交织的六十年代先锋场景原始面貌。文字仅为信息转载，缺乏个人聆听分析与艺术评价。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑收录了Arnold Dreyblatt两首现场录音作品，1997年分别于芝加哥Lounge Ax与苏黎世Theater Spektakel录制。A1'Point Source'以激发低音提琴为核心，融合鼓、吉他与小提琴，编制偏向室内即兴；A2'Lapse'则引入匈牙利扬琴cimbalom、萨克斯与电贝斯，呈现更为开放的声响场域。Table Of The Elements厂牌以小批量单面LP形式发行，纪念厂牌十周年，限量制作。作为美国实验音乐厂牌，合作阵容包括Jim O'Rourke、David Grubbs、Kevin Drumm等芝加哥实验圈重要人物，整体呈现学院派与即兴演奏交织的倾向，介于现代作曲与实验摇滚之间。

items.body: Review by alainPP — Przemysław Rudź trained on the sounds of Genesis, Yes, then Jarre, Tangerine Dream, and the master Schulze, whose music he often incorporates into his educational programs. Modern electronic soundscapes are combined with the traditional sounds of the Berlin School for an atmospheric 70s-80s fusion."Fight or Flight" is an electronic hit with a danceable, ethereal feel and vibrant synths. Reverberations, a voiceover, dynamic drums, and a guitar solo reminiscent of Tangerine Dream in the 80s create an energetic, futuristic radio edit that would ignite even the coldest atmosphere. "Pyramidion," with its syrupy, synth-heavy Roxy Music sound, has a strong Mandarin Dream vibe. It starts with a rhythmic feel before shifting into a repetitive ambient variation, a nod to "Thru Metamorphic Thru Rocks," which, despite Roman's guitar contribution, becomes tiresome and ultimately lacks a progressive spirit. "Two Faces of Autumn," an ethereal acoustic romance, evokes a Vangelis-esque atmosphere?icy and dreamlike. A solemn crescendo, the guitar tearing its notes from the velvety keyboard. Atmospheric, guaranteed relaxation, and the comfort of taking one's time. The finale is reminiscent of the haunting build-up in "Midnight Express.""Into the Higher Domain," a long, synthesized suite, a sonic manipulation of space, water, and the cerebral. The addition of wind instruments amplifies the airy feel. The guitar wanders with the wind, vibrating, a nod to Pink Floyd; a clear Vangelisian influence, a crystalline guitar with Asian-inspired vibrations, Proxima Centauri, where Roman launches into a reggae-prog solo, then flirts with new wave rock and psychedelic heavy pop. The highlight of this long, captivating track. "Watcher Of The Lies" is a stunning bonus track, a reimagining of this iconic Genesis song with a spacey synth feel. It's the kind of track you'll want to play on repeat, imagining it lasting forever.Przemysław Rudź and Roman Odoj bring a progressive sensibility to the music through their rhythmic contributions, effectively forming a quartet.
items._genre: progressive electronic / Berlin School / synth ambient
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑将柏林学派的序列合成器传统与七十至八十年代前卫摇滚的元素相融合，节奏层次丰富，音色在冷峻空灵与温暖旋律之间交替。Przemysław Rudziński 负责合成器架构与氛围铺陈，Roman Odoj 提供吉他即兴与律动支撑，使整体声音既具备舞曲化的推进力，又保留了环境音乐的呼吸感。曲目编排上，短篇作品以紧凑的电子化叙事为主，长篇组曲则展开更自由的器乐对话，融入爵士化的吉他独奏与新浪潮摇滚段落。专辑对 Genesis、Vangelis、Tangerine Dream 等前辈的引用十分明显，既构成其风格坐标，也限制了自身的原创辨识度。作为东欧独立厂牌的电子合辑，其制作水准扎实，适合作为柏林学派入门或跨界聆听的选择。

items.body: Ara is a three-track 8-minute mini-EP that spans a wide emotional and sonic range across three compositions, illustrating S. Salter’s evolving language of composition, which is detailed, emotive, and increasingly expansive in scope. Piano and production textures intertwine Ara is a three-track 8-minute mini-EP that spans a wide emotional and sonic range across three compositions, illustrating S. Salter’s evolving language of composition, which is detailed, emotive, and increasingly expansive in scope. A project by Amsterdam-based British artist Samuel Ruddick and Berlin-based Swiss artist Jeremia Reichen, this music places the piano at its core, with electronics used as subtle enhancements that add layers, texture, and droning color. The result is a luxuriously sparse journey into dreamlike realms of electronic art—beautifully unhurried and immersive.Opening track “Parts of Town” immediately sets the tone, drawing the listener into a cinematic world of orchestral textures and evolving dynamics, from a repeating phrase to a military snare beat, horns join for the march through town, there are kids playing in the street nearby. As the piece unfolds, layered arrangements build toward a restrained yet powerful climax, with brass entering to lift the track into its final movement before it slips away almost as quickly as it began.“Ara” follows as a brief, drifting interlude—fragmented and suspended—bridging the intensity of the opener with the warmth and richness of closing track “Sunday in Bloom.” Slow tall crystals forming ringing piano sparkles forming transparent layers of sound, here there is much bigger space to echo about in, while as ever nothing is urgent, everything is proceeding in delicious lazy afternoon time, just angels comfortably dozing. Piano and production textures intertwine to create a more expansive, reflective space, rounding out the EP’s emotional arc.In the three years since their acclaimed debut album Juun, S. Salter has steadily built a distinct presence. Alongside a live EP from their performance at Nxt Museum in Amsterdam and a contribution to Nils Frahm / Leiter Verlag’s official Piano Day compilation, Jeremia released a rework of their own track “Grove,” while Samuel composed the solo piano elegy “Robins.” Ara is available on Bandcamp and Apple Music.
items._genre: contemporary classical / ambient electronic / neo-classical piano
items._cn_summary: S. Salter 的《Ara》是一张三轨八分钟的迷你 EP，由阿姆斯特丹的英国艺术家与柏林的瑞士艺术家合作完成。作品以钢琴为核心，电子元素作为微妙增强层叠加其中，营造出稀疏而奢华的梦境氛围。开篇曲融合管弦乐质感、军鼓节奏与铜管号声，呈现电影感叙事结构；同名曲作为碎片化的漂浮间奏；终曲则展开更广阔的反射空间，钢琴与制作纹理交织出慵懒午后般的回响。整体风格延续了当代古典与氛围电子的融合脉络，编曲精细而不紧迫，但文本中存在明显重复段落，且音乐本身的实验边界相对收敛，偏向精致氛围构建而非激进创新。

items.body: Detroit deathgaze duo VAZUM will cross the Atlantic this summer for a UK tour while Zach Pliska and Emily Sturm put the final touches on their next full-length album. Since the release of 2024’s Western Violence, the band has further retreated into the borderlands between goth rock, shoegaze, deathrock, and serrated post-punk pressure. Built around Pliska and Sturm’s shared vision, VAZUM operate from their own Light Echo Studio with the self-reliance of a band that has learned to make limitation feel like voltage. Their music comes hard and grand, with blown-out guitars, cold vocal interplay, martial drums, and a taste for grandeur that never sands off the threat at the edges. They call it deathgaze, and the name fits: heavy-lidded, severe, beautiful in the way broken glass can be beautiful when the light catches it at the wrong angle. VAZUM have been moving steadily through the US and Europe, building their reputation through rousing live performances rather than the machinery of a larger industry apparatus. The band remain rooted in a DIY ethos, working outside the usual channels while carrying their songs into rooms where volume, atmosphere, and physical presence still mean something. The upcoming UK run begins June 24 in Edinburgh and continues through Newcastle upon Tyne, Leicester, London, Oxford, Bristol, Coventry, Leeds, and Salford. Tickets and show information are available through the band’s official channels. Tickets and show info can be found here. items._cn_summary: 这是一篇关于底特律二人组VAZUM英国巡演的资讯文章。乐队由Zach Pliska和Emily Sturm组成，自2024年发行《Western Violence》以来持续在哥特摇滚、自赏、死亡摇滚与后朋克之间的模糊地带深耕。音乐以失真吉他、冷峻的人声交织、军事化鼓点为骨架，呈现出粗粝而宏大的质感。乐队在自建的Light Echo Studio录音，保持DIY精神与独立运作模式，巡演场次密集，从爱丁堡一路延伸至萨尔福德。文章详细列出了九场演出的日期与场地信息，并附有社交媒体链接。整体而言，这是一篇标准格式的巡演公告，对乐队音乐风格有一定描述，但深度有限，更偏向新闻发布而非深度乐评。

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album

. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?

items._cn_summary: 这是丹麦三人组合GuldGanger的首张数字EP，由北欧民谣场景中经验丰富的歌手Mia Guldhammer领衔。五首曲目以传统民谣为主，成员各自带来不同的音乐视角。开场曲《Svennedal》以粗犷的小跑节奏展示了Guldhammer极具说服力的嗓音；口簧与风笛为唯一原创曲目《Nordgård》提供了持续推进的动力。钦巴龙（cimbalom）为传统曲目《Agnete Of Bjergmanden》增添了细腻的背景层次，而终曲《Ormsø》作为器乐曲融合了口簧、长笛和弦乐，营造出既令人兴奋又略带失衡的独特氛围。整体氛围古朴而略带粗粝感，展现出乐队超越新人水准的成熟度。

items.body: After nine previous albums and a 25-year career at the forefront of world music, Lucas Santtana is fluent in the many genres of Brazilian music. His new project, Brasiliano , is a musical exploration of the languages of Brazil. With songs sung in Portuguese, French, English, Spanish, Occitan, Cape Verde Creole, and Tupy-Guarani, a Brazilian native language, Santtana has assembled guest lyricists and vocalists representing a range of musical and linguistic influences. The result is a warm and compelling musical treatise on the diverse cultural history of Brazil, expressed through the Brazilian variant of Portuguese, best described as Brasiliano. Returning to his roots, the opening cut and lead single �A hist�ria de nossa l�ngua� features Gilberto Gil, a national treasure with whom Santtana worked early in his career. As the liner notes explain, Brasiliano , the language, is depicted in the song as a feminine character meeting other people (languages) on her travels, tracing the history of the language as an offshoot of Latin, including �Occitan, Celtic, Galician, Portuguese, Mozarabic, and others. The chorus features Indigenous words that are part of everyday Brazilian culture: Itapu�, Ipanema, Maracan�, Capoeira, etc.� This song acts as a sort of abstract for the dissertation to follow. Santtana and Gil call and respond over what has become the composer�s trademark mixture of detailed, layered, human-played instruments, including on this track violins and violas, piano, guitars, mellotron, and synths. Throughout the record, Santtana creates an inviting effect with a contemporary gloss, combined with the warm resonance of wood, drum skins, wire strings, sticks, bows, and voices. The album features a range of styles, from the lively party track �Ver meu povo se abra�ar� to the convincing reggae of the second single, �Que seja um reggae�. With sophisticated songcraft and inspired arrangements, the songs remain inviting and accessible. Brasiliano by Lucas Santtana Fitting with the theme of the interrelationships among languages, Brasiliano is a celebration of international collaboration. For example, �Independ�ncia� features Karyna Gomes, a singer from Guinea-Bissau; Anglo-French performer Piers Faccini sings �Battre des ailes� accompanied by an appropriately French-sounding accordion; and popular Brazilian singer Flavia Coelho is featured on �Dans le sud feat�. The gentle �Strati di tempo� is the closest to Santtana�s earliest singer/guitarist style, with Italian star Dimartino taking the lead vocals. Brasiliano by Lucas Santtana Language is culture; so too are politics. And with the involvement of Gilberto Gill, who served as Minister of Culture in President Luiz In�cio Lula da Silva�s government and was jailed and exiled for his political affiliations in the 1960s, it is no surprise that this album is overtly political.� For example, on �L�nguas Gerais,� French rapper Oxmo Puccino �speaks about colonization.� Continuing to quote from the liner notes, �Indigenous languages and cultures in South America were buried under European colonization.� Tainara Takua and Oxmo Puccino sing �Cocanha� in Occitan. Their music is part of a movement to prevent this endangered romance language from dying out.� � Like his popular previous recording O Para�so (2023), which was concerned with the environment, Brasiliano is a concept album that explores the role of linguistics in culture. And like on O Para�so , Santtana is never preachy. The high-minded intellectual roots of the project are made palatable by the creative and appealing music assembled to tell the story. It is a message of inclusion, collaboration, and the joy of our shared occupancy in this place and at this time. With many languages, many musical styles, and the artistry of many talented and effective musical partners, Brasiliano is a remarkable achievement in curation and musical skill with a compelling contemporary message. items.body:
How do you celebrate 50 years of music by a band that blazed trails for the charged, hypnotic pizzica sound, breaking it out of its homeland in southern Italy? How do you look afresh at a sound that�s changed and broadened its appeal without ever abandoning its roots as a new generation took over the instruments? It�s a challenge, but what Canzionere Grecanico Salentino (CGS) have done is reframe some of the pieces from those earlier decades through the lens of those playing and singing the songs now.
The brainchild of Rina and Daniele Durante, early CGS avidly proudly staked out its territory as champions of an almost forgotten culture. In the hands of their son, fiddler/frame drummer and singer Mauro Durante, the original vision has gone global (he also has a successful duo with guitarist Justin Adams) and they�ve become a major name in world music for their energy and outstanding musicality. They�ve made people in so many countries believe in the pizzica. One big milestone acceptance came with working alongside the celebrated pianist Ludovico Einaudi on his
Taranta
project in 2014, which gave them an even wider reach and boosted them even high. Very aptly, a remix and remastering of the �Taranta� track with him is included.
In a world that loves to dance, this is dance music with depth and power that explodes out of the speakers. It honors the material from the past while keeping its eyes firmly fixed on the future, clasping hands across the generations to celebrate the band and its lauded history.
Il Mito
(The Myth) pays homage without ever being slavish. There�s a real, urgent energy to the music-making here.
The title cut was written by the older Durantes, a cornerstone of CGS�s early repertoire and a reflection on life in their part of Italy. Roberto Licci comes to sing with his son Emanuele. Early vocalist Rossella Pinto reprises her role on �Lu Rusciu De Lu Mare.� Yet this isn�t all hearkening to the past. The sounds have taken on new colors and arrangements as younger fingers play them. It�s still mostly acoustic, with a few electric touches like a synth bass to round out the sound.
This is still completely Italian music, the enveloping, dry sound of pizzica, something that�s evolved over the last half-century, moving from a regional to a global stage. The band, and their compositions, deserve the party, but it begs the question:
Where will all this be in another 50 years?

items.body: W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes This collaboration between the five-piece Belgian instrumental group W�r, whose members specialize in bringing the music of earlier centuries to life, and Kongero, the acclaimed Swedish female acapella folk quartet, offers an unusual chance to explore how their two cultures, ostensibly so different, can come together. It might sounds an unlikely mix, but here�s a spoiler: it turns out they�re pretty much musical best friends. The album kicks off at a cracking pace with �Var �r Du?�, a bravura performance through a twisted, tortuous piece that manages to be both elegant and surprising. However, the true astonishment arrives at the end, when the audience applauds and you suddenly realize this was recorded live (actually over two separate performances). W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes The musicians bring material from their separate traditions, plus one original, showcasing their skills in intricate, swinging arrangements for both instruments and voices. Thanks to their skill, the varied ideas fit together seamlessly so it�s brimming with delights, like the wonderfully-titled �Drinking Like A Sweet Swede,� where the singers layers their harmonies over a jaunty backing. Everything is intricate, performed with a glowing precision that can disarm the senses with its beauty. The highlight, perhaps, is the beautiful �Klosterjungfrun.� The slow, seductive opening draws in the listener, the voices airy and light, curling around each other as the instruments wind long their path their. It�s a beautiful piece, but really, just one gem among so many here. W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes There�s never a foot wrong, no note out of place and the performances are passionate, stellar, a true collaboration of instruments and voices. Add to that a mix that�s sharp as a razor, and Songbooks Live is a truly outstanding album, a perfect illustration that people have more in common than separates them. And it illustrates exactly what artists can achieve live. With luck, they�ll work together again. Soon, please. Find the artists online. items.body: Echo by Emi Makabe L oss galvanizes, loss focuses, and musical artists turn loss into shared reflections. Emi Makabe has focused the passing of her father into a generous meditation on resilience and legacy with her second recording on Sunnyside Records, Echo . The title reminds us of the connections between generations. Here are ten musical memories that span time and culture, blending a modern jazz sensibility with a traditional Japanese soul. Born in Japan, where she studied Japanese traditional music, Emi Makabe moved to New York in 2008. She is an educator and contributor to the jazz scene, composing and performing her own music. Her previous recordings, an EP on the Japanese Jazz label D-Musica Out of Time (2016) and Anniversary (2020), laid the foundation of her sound: soaring, sweet singing in Japanese, English and wordless vocalizing, accompanied by her flute and shamisen on top of jazz-inspired piano, drums, and double bass. Using these materials, Makabe celebrates the legacy of her father, supported by Thomas Morgan (double bass, backing vocals) and Vitor Gon�alves (piano, accordion, Wurlitzer electric piano), both of whom return from her previous records, as well as Kenny Wollesen (drums, percussion, vibraphone, electronics). Also appearing as guests are Meshell Ndegeocello (spoken word), Jason Moran (piano), and Bill Frisell (acoustic guitar) on the opening track. Echo by Emi Makabe Opening with Frisell�s acoustic guitar and confidently sentimental, �Birthday Song� comes to grips with loss, featuring a touching spoken meditation and a haunting Frisell solo. It ends with the hope, �I wanna remember the warmth of being in your arms.� The record closes with �Overture,� anchored by Gon�alves� dripping Wurlitzer supporting Makabe�s Japanese exhortation, �Let's talk again, countless times/Let's talk, if we meet again.� Echo by Emi Makabe Besides the refreshingly unselfconscious sentimentality, Makabe strides confidently between the traditional Japanese melodies, instruments, and the language of her upbringing in her father�s world and the contemporary jazz of New York clubs. �Snow� begins with Makabe�s shamisen playing a pentatonic tune, while �Text� swings in a fast bebop, with Makabe�s flute and harmonized Japanese scat singing. Echo by Emi Makabe �Morisan� hurries between worlds led by bouncy accordion, rolling jazz traps, and a stylish piano solo by Jason Moran. Moran also shares production credits with Thomas Morgan and Makabe herself. Utterly unique in approach, and equipped with a lovely vocal instrument, and with a skilled and single-minded ensemble, Emi Makabe has created a passionate, introspective, and honest fusion of tradition and modernity to celebrate the passing of the generations. Find the artist online. Further listening: Carmen Souza - The Silver Messengers: A Tribute to Horace Silver Mamak Khadem - Rembrance Yussef Dayes - Black Classical Music

items._cn_summary: 这是Emi Makabe在Sunnyside Records发行的第二张专辑，围绕其父亲离世的主题，以十首曲目追溯跨代际的文化记忆。她生于日本，曾系统学习日本传统音乐，2008年移居纽约后融入当代爵士圈，因而在作品中自如穿梭于日本传统旋律、五声音阶与纽约俱乐部爵士语汇之间。演奏配置以低音提琴、钢琴/瓦尔特电钢、鼓为主轴，她本人演唱日语、英语及无歌词人声，并演奏尺八与三味线。Bill Frisell在开场曲贡献原声吉他与独奏，Meshell Ndegeocello以口语念白参与，Jason Moran在另一曲担任钢琴独奏。作品从三味线五声音阶开篇的《Snow》到快速bebop风格的《Text》与手风琴驱动的《Morisan》，展示了传统与现代之间的灵活切换。整体呈现是一种真诚、内省的文化融合，既保留日本传统音乐的根基，也承接当代爵士的和声与即兴逻辑。

items.body: West Virginia Snake Handler Revival �They Shall Take Up Serpents� by Sublime Frequencies M cDowell County West Virginia is nestled in the Appalachian Mountains, and is both stunning and isolated. But, since coal�s heyday has long past, it is also considered the poorest part of the state, if not the entire country. With perhaps as much as 30% unemployment and low average annual incomes, it, like much of the coal regions that surround it, is horrifyingly depressed. It is also overwhelmingly white, and went hard for Trump, boasting the largest support for him in the country in 2016. In 2023, The Guardian ran a photo exhibit on what was designated to be West Virginia�s �last snake handling church.� The photos, taken at The House of Lord Jesus, in Squire, deep in McDowell County�s claustrophobic, coal scarred southwest, depict stark black and white images of an elderly woman burning a kerosene flame near her face, lots of snakes, and people seemingly possessed as they surrender to a form of Pentecostal practice that uses a quote from Mark 16:18 as their raison d'�tre. �They shall take up serpents�,� the verse claims. And the church�s members do, sometimes handling groups of venomous rattlers at once, bouncing uncontrollably, occasionally being bit, now and again dying from the poison. But in The Guardian�s photo exhibit, there are also occasional shots of a guitar player. And it�s the music, from this very church, that not only accompanies this endangered, radical Christian practice, but which is also the focus of Sublime Frequencies� West Virginia Snake Handler Revival , the first album the Seattle-based label has ever released featuring music recorded in the United States. Not surprisingly, Ian Brennan, known for recordings of music made by endangered communities all over the globe, produced this record. And despite these folks� feudal views on homosexuals and women, musically, this is likely some of the most over the top, hypnotic rock and roll transcendence to ever be captured on tape. �He is #1� is the ultimate proof. The track, led by the frantic, in-the-red vocals of Pastor Chris Wolford, features guitars and drums chugging out a monotonous one-chord vamp covered in swamp muck. They chew on that chord, cranking a possessed telecaster-infused, amplified stomp out into the hollers, driving with a stamina that would make Junior Kimbrough proud. Wolford, undoubtedly drenched in sweat, hollers, whoops, insinuates, and punctuates every phrase with �huh,� as is typical for hardcore preachers all over the southern US. At 13 minutes, it�s nearly too much to bear. There�s a reason this is the album�s final track. West Virginia Snake Handler Revival "They Shall Take Up Serpents" by Sublime Frequencies But there are plenty of other examples of this album�s disturbing power. The opening track, the one minute �Spirit of God,� features Wolford�s voice, a capella, doused in echo, as if he�s testifying deep within an abandoned mine shaft. �Jesus Has to be #1,� is not unlike the LP�s finale, though it�s much shorter. Here, Wolford screams �Aah Gawd,� and it�s terrifying. Elsewhere, other people sing, with haunted, determined results. The vocalist on �I�m a Lord Jesus Man� is never on key, and the music is better for it. Here is the style of many a 1960s or 70s-era trucker anthem, complete with slithering guitar licks and grooves made for the highway. Later, Wolford returns, exhorting about forgetting to take his ADHD meds and instead getting jacked up on Starbucks. He screams, pants, and grunts, nearly obliterating the wall of electric thrum behind him. Some of the intensity found here is manipulated. The brief track, �Rock and Roll was stolen from God by Satan,� for example, features anonymous testimony over a guitar and drum loop. �Maybe I Won�t Do What I Said I�d Do� loops the title repeatedly over a duplicated demonic laugh for 22 seconds. But by and large, Brennan left the tapes alone, leaving the music�s pugnaciousness be. West Virginia Snake Handler Revival �They Shall Take Up Serpents� by Sublime Frequencies Nothing here was created for commercial purposes. Instead, it documents a music that hasn�t budged stylistically in 50 years, rampaging somewhere between hillbilly boogie, and rock and roll choogle. It�s a natural, amplified soundtrack to small congregations of people whose practice has connections to other deep, unyielding trance ritual around the globe, from Gnawa in Morocco, to ecstatic nightclub DJs in Berlin, to the electrified molam that accompanies the Phi Ta Khon festival of ghosts in NE Thailand. Further reading: Peni Candra Rini - Wani Alhousseini Anivolla & Girum Mezmur - Afropentatonism Photo documentary in The Guardian Hear more of the album.

items._genre: sacred music / Pentecostal rock / field recording / American roots
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Sublime Frequencies发行，是该西雅图独立厂牌首度在美国本土录制的田野录音作品，制作人Ian Brennan以记录濒危文化音乐著称。录制地点位于西弗吉尼亚州麦道威尔县深山中一座五旬节派蛇礼教堂，牧师Chris Wolford带领信众在单和弦嗡鸣中以放克节奏般的电吉他与鼓点反复碾压十三分钟，伴以汗水浸透的狂野呼喊与即兴嚎叫。整张专辑将这种源于阿巴拉契亚煤乡、充满宗教狂热的原始摇滚灵歌完整保留，作品既具备人类学田野录音的文献价值，也在声音层面呈现出催眠般的迷幻张力，与Junior Kimbrough式的密西西比催眠布鲁斯血脉相连。

items.body: Tribute to Bantoma Sanogo , on of the historic masters of this music. Hunter Folk Vol II: Tribute to Bantoma Sanogo by Pelengana Blo December, 2025 Dorothy Moskowitz gets to the heart of the 21st Century in this satiric story of a robot's devotion in this song from Five Day Miracle Tent Crusade . I�m your puppet, I�m your mimic I copy your copy and you call me a clone Simulating a heart and emotional tone Why can�t you think any better, any better of me When I�m full-on devoted to the human that you seem to be? Confession (The Robot Song) feat. Dorothy Moskowitz by FIVE DAY MIRACLE TENT CRUSADE October, 2025 Tone of Voice Orchestra always musically surprises, and lyrically makes you think, even with the simplicity of a song like this from their new album. One domino onto the next That�s how castles crumble Running from the Devil by Tone of Voice Orchestra Some very rootsy string and percussion music by The Kasambwe Brothers from Malawi, Africa. They are street musicians in their home village of Ndirande, with an acoustic guitar, a babatone (a bass banjo or ngoni, of sorts) and a drum kit of animal skins stretched on pots and pans, with bottle caps shakers. The Kasambwe Brothers by The Kasambwe Brothers Released October, 2025 Here's a reissue of a classic roots-fusion recording from Brazil. Percussionist Marco Bosco recorded Metalmadeira in 1983, bringing the still evolving world of elecronic music into his more traditional interest in Brazilian rhythms. It still sounds fresh to me all these years later. Metalmadeira by Marco Bosco, Ruria Duprat Reissue: 2025 And here's a preview of his new album, Metalmadeira II . He's joined on this one by the trio Alter Disco Metalmadeira II by Marco Bosco, Alter Disco Coming in November, 2025 Kapela Rej is a group performing traditional Belarusian music. From their album Da Šatajsia, Soniejka: Belarusian Music , this song was recorded live at a festival in Zrenjanin, Serbia, performed on the duda (Belarusian bagpipe) and the violin. Da �atajsia, Soniejka: Belarusian Music by Kapela Rej (feat. Sergi Llena) Released in August of 2025 There's really no rule that says these internet 'playlists' have to be new material. Just like my radio show, there's decades of great artists and bands out there. The Cypriot band Monsieur Doumani has been a hit around here since their first album, Grippy Grappa . Here's two songs (with links to our reviews) from Pissourin (2021) and Sikoses (2015). Pissourin by Monsieur Doumani Sikoses (2015) by Monsieur Doumani Martha Mavroidi 's Portaki (2013) was reviewed by Greg Harness, who wrote, "It�s certainly a folky jazz, or maybe a jazzy folk. Mavroidi describes her music as a �blending folk melodies with jazz harmony and improvisation� Portaki by Martha Mavroidi The New Eves offer challenging music that skirts a 1000 years of tradition, ancient balladry through folk, rock and punk of the modern era. Read Chris Nickson's review in RootsWorld. The New Eve Is Rising by The New Eves August, 2025 In memory of the great accordionist, Flaco Jimenez , here's one of the editor's favorites, from one of his many recordings with Max Baca. Flaco & Max: Legends & Legacies by Flaco Jim�nez & Max Baca Released 2014 The incredible 50 year journey of The Mahotella Queens, possibly the most famous singing group from South Africa, with 83 year old Hilda Tloubatla still at the front of the trio, backed by a solid band that echoes the Soweto sound of the 70s and 80s. Here's a track form their new album, Buya Buya: Come Back . Buya Buya: Come Back by Mahotella Queens A summer treat from one of RW's favorite ensembles in 2025, Tako Toki. Read more about their full album from earlier in the year in RootsWorld. BADASS by Tako Toki August, 2025 A Zero Nove Nove Playlist Some of the artists mentioned in our interview with Giuseppe Bortone Onde by Maria Mazzotta Culla e Tempesta by Faraualla Gathering of Enchanted Herbs EP by Sekvoya Curannera by Yar�k� La Novia by La Cantiga de la Serena In his review of the 2019 release by this duo from Malawi Bruce Miller wrote, "Homemade instruments such as the ones played on this record seem like orchestras. The guitar holds tight to the rhythm while Ythe long-necked, banjo-like babatoni , the sliding bass sound serves as bottom end as well as lead. While key shifts are few, dynamics, subtleties, and variety seem endless. And their vocal harmonies are like choruses... there simply are no weak spots." Here's the single from their 2025 album that comes out in June of 2025. Ma Gitala by Madalitso Band Well, it's not really roots, in spite of its bluesey enough sound. But Geiger von M�ller 's "Alien Fig Yogurt Incident" is charmingly weird and musically more complex than you might think at first. And his videos are out-of-this- world . Italian composer Fabio Mina explores the contemporary possibilities of that most ancient of instruments, the flute, in less than ancient settings and methods on Existence / Resistance . Fabio Mina - Existence / Resistance by Okum January, 2025 Ebo Taylor, Adrian Younge & Ali Shaheed Muhammad are touring the world right now with a new round of what they call "psychedelic afrobeat." The album is titled Ebo Taylor , honoring the 88 year oldGhanaian musician's years as one of highlife music's greatest artsists/ Ebo Taylor JID022 by Ebo Taylor, Adrian Younge, Ali Shaheed Muhammad March, 2025 We've been covering some great Polish music this month, and here's another to hear. Daj Ognia is one a radio listener tipped me off to, a band with roots in both Poland and Scandinavia. This is from their 2023 album, Przedn�wek . Siwy kon, siwy kon, Na siwego siadom, A swojego dam dziadom Gray horse, gray horse, I'll sit on the gray one, And I'll give mine to the grandfathers Przedn�wek by Daj Ognia Released 2023 "Sarah Allen and company should be commended for crafting an instantly recognizable sound that expands the boundaries of instrumental acoustic music." - Lee Blackstone in RootsWorld. Flook just released a single from their upcoming 2025 album, and it is as artful as expected. Here's a taste of Sanju . The Farther Shore/Winter Flower - Single by Flook Single is out January, 2025. Full album in March. The French trio Tako Toki create all their music on instruments made from found objects and scrap they collect and make musicial. It's a clever idea that's been done before, but they take it to a different level, moving from the dead serious, to the slyly imitative, to the downright funny, like this homage to the movie sound track and sound effects artist, Raymond Scott. We have a review coming soon, but dig in and enjoy some now. HIRSUTES FARFELUS - LP by Tako Toki February 2025 Clarinet virtuoso Aur�lie Charneux leads a trio of musicians on Cinqui�me Saison . Joined by Nicolas Puma (double bass) and Simon Leleux (percussion), her compositions explore a 5th season of sounds, improvising to evoke the relationship between humans and nature, the earth and its human adversaries and friends. It can be trance like and soothing, or harsh and demanding. Cinqui�me Saison by Aur�lie Charneux, Simon Leleux, Nicolas Puma This is the second album by Lib�rica , led by bassist Manel Forti� (a favorite around here). It brings together Catalan singers Pere Mart�nez, Valencian Carles D�nia and C�diz-born Antonio Lizana, along with trumpeter and vocalist Alba Careta. It's jazz at its heart, and tradtion in its soul. (Read our review of Manel Forti� & Magli Sare's album 2022 release, re�tornar .) AL� - Iberian Chants by Lib�rica Novalima is a team of DJ-musicians from Lima, Peru who dig deeper into their own roots while staying firmly on the dancefloor. La Danza (Deluxe Version) by NOVALIMA January, 2025 Digital Ngoma is group of musicians from the Indian Ocean island of Mayotte who experiment with traditional beats and electronics. They guarantee "100% made in Mayotte." Digital Ngoma Vol.2 by Kim Canadian string player (mostly mandola and mandolin) Kevin Breit is joined by singer Ariana Gillis on one of the few covers of a Warren Zevon song that has ever been successful and original. I Love You by Kevin Breit Released in 2021 Orchestre Tout Puissant Marcel Duchamp is possibly the best named band in Europe: artful, enigmatic and surprising at every turn. We'll have a review of this soon, but here's a taste of their newest album. While you wait, you can read Martha Willette Lewis' review of their previous album, We're OK. But We're Lost Anyway to get the lowdon on who they are. Ventre unique by Orchestre Tout Puissant Marcel Duchamp January, 2025 We just reviewed Lynn Adib 's 2024 work with Zeid Hamdan, as the duo Bedouin Burger . Here's a taste of some of her solo work, from her 2018 album Youmma . YOUMMA by Lynn Adib Posted January 2025 Wishamalii is an adventurous trio based in Helsinki: singer, oud player and composer Nemat Battah (Palestine/Jordan), pianistand composer Kari Ikonen and Ethiopian-born, Finland-based percussionist Abdissa �Mamba� Assefa (Ethipia). Their newest work, Al-Bahr is rooted in classical Arab music but only as a starting point for new compositions. Ikonen has even refined a piano tuning to play the maqam notes at the heart of this music. Wishamalii - Al-Bahr by Nordic Notes September, 2024 We'll have a review shortly from this album by Polish cymbaly and accordion player Karolina Wegrzyn , but here's a taste of it, a traditional Carpatho-Rusin song that translates as "Whose scythe cuts well." Oy Vesna Krasna by Karolina Wegrzyn January 2025 Two Italians and a Belgian come together in Brussels... sounds like the beginning of a joke, I know. But the sounds that come fromthe instruments, voices and hearts of Flavia Clementi (vocals, shruti box, percussion), Federico Bragetti (cello, vocals, percussion) and Thomas Van Bogaert (guitar, vocals, percussion) is serious, joyous and absobs all the influences a city like Brussels seems to embrace. items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — After crafting an energetic and avant-garde mix of symphonic black and death metal laced with gothand folk on its debut release "Schizo Level," the Portuguese metal band THANATOSCHIZO immediatelyshifted gears on its sophomore release INSOMNIOUSNIGHTLIFT which jettisoned all of the black metalaspects and relegated the death metal style to only the occasional midrange grunt in a doomiercontext. In their stead came more influences from 70s progressive rock, 90s gothic metal and a moregroove-based death doom plodding style. While the band added Miguel Angelo on bass, this time aroundthe long list of guest musicians that added horns, trumpet sounds, ethnic samples and otherdecorative features were clearly absent on this more cohesive unit.While never as popular as fellow Portuguese act Moonspell, THANATOSCHIZO was very much out of thesame playbook at this point as it drifted into a more atmospheric darkened style of progressive gothmetal that featured both clean male and female vocal styles along with the death metal carry overfrom album #1. Noticeably less experimental than "Schizoid Level," this second offering featured 10tracks but clocked in at a whopping near 67 minutes which makes this one seem more like a doublealbum. Delving further into the progressive realms, INSOMIOUSNIGHTLIFT is a concept album based onthe sleeping disorders of the band's lead vocalists and is designed to be one of those free flowingcontinuous pieces of music where the tracks coalesce to make a larger experience however this istheoretical and the album sounds like a bunch of individual tracks to my ears.The album immediately distinguishes itself from its predecessor with a lush atmospheric intro on"Reminder" which slowly drifts into existence and allows the band to display its new chill out gothapproach before allowing the groovy death doom to plod in however the album isn't free of feistymetallic furor either as it alternates between slow meandering passages that give way to energeticoutbursts but sound more like groove metal with death metal decor than actual death metal itself. Amore streamlined album of sort, the creativity had also been tamped down and demoted offering a morestandard progressive goth metal trajectory. While the male can cover both clean and growly vocalsquite well, the female is fairly limited to a one trick pony style reminding me of the girl inAyreon which is more of a folk singing style than metal which i find a bit put offy. Overall i find this second release a lot less interesting than the crafty debut which really knewhow to throw curveballs and of course the extra bombastic black metal and death metal in cahootsmade that a true metallic feast while this more subdued version of the band sounds a bit trendy asif they listened to some Type O Negative or even Moonspell and aimed for the more commercialapproach. Whatever the case it's a decent album for what it is but lacks the interesting elementsthat made the band stand out. Overall the album is too bloated and not creative enough to warrant a67 minute playing time and half way through pretty much loses my interest. It's a good album butit's too bad the band didn't stay true to the style developed on its debut because that one isreally a creative gem of the Portuguese metal underground.
items._genre: gothic metal / progressive metal / death doom
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是葡萄牙乐队THANATOSCHIZO的第二张作品，相比首张的前卫交响黑死金属风格有明显转向。黑金属元素被彻底剥离，70年代前卫摇滚与90年代哥特金属的影响占据主导，加上groove律动的死亡厄运沉重推进。专辑围绕主唱们的睡眠障碍概念展开，尝试将十首曲目串联为统一的流动体验，但在乐评听来更像独立曲目的集合。制作上邀请了贝斯手Miguel Angelo固定加入，乐器编制比首张精简，去掉了大量客座乐手带来的号角、民族采样等装饰元素，呈现更紧凑的整体感。人声配置采用男女双主唱，男性兼顾清声与死腔咆哮，女性则以民谣唱法贯穿。乐评认为相比首张的丰富实验性与转折球，这张的创造力被刻意收敛，趋向标准化的渐进哥特金属路径，声音上带有Type O Negative与Moonspell的影子。整体仍具一定完成度但缺乏令人惊喜的突破点。

items.body: Alif Hilal, formerly known as Lyra Pramuk, takes us through the dizzying mixture of influences that fed into last year's album Hymnal and a new rework called Hymnal (Resung), from rave to blues via devotional music, minimalism, folk song and more (the results are compiled into a playlist exclusively for tQ Subscriber Plus tier members) Photo by Cy Klock Music journalists love to tell you they know all the influences that has gone into a new album, but a lot of the time the artists responsible themselves are left baffled by these comparisons. We thought, why not go straight to the source? Alif Hilal (fka Lyra Pramuk) is a composer and vocalist who uses electronic processing to stretch, contort and reimagine acoustic sources... The post Guest Playlist: Alif Hilal appeared first on The Quietus.
items._genre: experimental electronic / vocal processing / contemporary classical / minimalism
items._cn_summary: 本文并非传统乐评，而是一篇以歌单推荐为载体的艺术家自述。Alif Hilal（原名Lyra Pramuk）以作曲家与声乐家的双重身份，通过电子处理技术对人声进行拉伸、扭曲与重构，将原声素材转化为实验性声响。专辑《Hymnal》及其重制版《Hymnal (Resung)》融合了锐舞、布鲁斯、礼拜音乐、极简主义与民歌等多元元素，展现出跨类型的美学拼贴。文字着重呈现影响来源的杂糅性，突出口头传统与电子手段之间的张力。整体内容偏简介性质，缺少对具体作品结构或声音设计的深入分析，信息密度有限。

items._cn_summary: 本文并非传统乐评，而是来自个人收藏记录的唱片信息摘录，完整罗列了John Cale的《Stainless Gamelan: Inside The Dream Syndicate Volume III》专辑的厂牌、版本、曲目时长、演奏者与制作人员等元数据。专辑收录了1960年代中后期由Tony Conrad从档案录音中整理并制作的三张系列唱片中的第三张，曲目包括电钢琴、无品吉他、磁带操作与中提琴等实验性器乐作品，融合了简约主义、持续音与磁带音乐手法，呈现出极简且具有冥想气质的声音探索。该文以纯粹的元数据为主，未涉及任何音乐评价或审美分析，因此无法作为乐评提供价值，但所记录的专辑本身与极简、实验、磁带音乐等小众风格高度契合，发行厂牌为独立小厂牌Table Of The Elements。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Erling Wold为Jon Jost导演电影《The Bed You Sleep In》创作的原创配乐，1993年由小厂牌Table Of The Elements发行。作品以钢琴为核心，辅以大提琴、单簧管、萨克斯、手风琴与鼓等乐器配置，呈现出介于现代古典与电影配乐之间的气质。十二首曲目多为短篇结构，标题如《孤独的慰藉》《悲伤》《Jean已逝》等带有叙事性，暗示作品与电影情节的紧密关联。整体偏向简约、沉思的氛围，弦乐与管乐的对位处理体现出当代作曲的技法。作为一部独立电影配乐，它在小众实验厂牌的语境下具有一定的探索性，但作品本身更接近氛围化的场景音乐，缺乏强烈的实验突破或跨类型融合力度。对于关注当代古典与实验音乐边缘地带的声音爱好者而言，这是一份值得了解的档案式聆听材料。

items.body: Zeena Parkins6 languagesFrom Wikipedia, the free encyclopediaZeena ParkinsParkins on April 5, 2008Background informationBorn1956 (age 69–70)Detroit, Michigan, U.S.GenresExperimentalfree improvisationavant-gardeOccupationsMusiciancomposerInstrumentsHarpaccordionkeyboardsomnichordYears active1980s–presentLabelsTzadikGood Child MusicRelative PitchTable of the ElementsCase Study RecordsWebsitewww.zeenaparkins.comZeena Parkins (born 1956) is an American composer and multi-instrumentalist active in experimental, free improvised, contemporary classical, and avant-jazz music; she is known for having "reinvented the harp".[1] Parkins performs on standard harps, several custom electric harps, piano, and accordion. She was a 2019 Guggenheim Fellow and professor in the Music Department at Mills College.[2]Life and career[edit]Born in 1956 in Detroit, Michigan, Parkins studied at Bard College and moved to New York City in 1984.[3] Her work ranges from solo performance to large ensembles.[2] Besides standard and electric harps, her work also incorporates Foley, field recordings, analog synthesizers, samplers, oscillators and homemade instruments.She has recorded six solo harp records[2] and recorded and performed with Björk,[4] Matmos, Ikue Mori, Fred Frith, Tom Cora, Christian Marclay, Yoko Ono,[5] John Zorn (including in Cobra performances),[3] Chris Cutler, Pauline Oliveros,[6] Nels Cline,[7] Elliott Sharp,[8] Lee Ranaldo,[9] Butch Morris,[10] Tin Hat Trio,[11] William Winant,[12] Anthony Braxton, Bobby Previte,[13] Courtney Love's band Hole,[14] and others. She has also been a member of a number of experimental rock bands, including No Safety,[15] News from Babel,[16] and Skeleton Crew.[3]Parkins worked with dance companies and choreographers, including the John Jasperse Company, Jennifer Monson,[17] Neil Greenberg, and Emmanuelle Vo-Dinh, and has won three Bessie Awards for her achievement in composition for dance.[2]She provided scores for filmmakers including Abigail Child,[18] Isabella Rossellini,[19] and Cynthia Madansky.[20][2]Parkins received a 1997 Foundation for Contemporary Arts Grants to Artists Award.[21]Discography[edit]As leader[edit]Release yearTitleLabelAdditional personnel1987Something Out ThereNo Man's LandSam Bennett, Cora, Wayne Horvitz, Christian Marclay, Jim Mineses, Ikue Mori, James Staley1992Ursa's DoorLes Disques VictoMori, Chris Cochrane, Sara Parkins, Maggie Parkins1993Nightmare AlleyTable of the Elements1995IsabelleAvantS. items._cn_summary: 此文并非传统意义的乐评，而是从维基百科摘抄的Zeena Parkins个人简介及唱片列表。文章介绍了这位美国作曲家和多乐器演奏家的生平等信息：她以"重新发明竖琴"著称，使用标准竖琴、定制电竖琴、钢琴、手风琴以及自制乐器进行创作，活跃于实验、自由即兴、当代古典与前卫爵士领域。她曾与Björk、John Zorn、Fred Frith、Yoko Ono、Anthony Braxton等众多艺术家合作，作品涵盖独奏到大型乐团编制，并涉及舞蹈配乐与电影配乐。文章罗列了其作为领队的多张专辑，但未对任何作品进行实质性的音乐分析或评价，缺乏评论深度，作为乐评信息严重不足。

items._cn_summary: Zeena Parkins 的《Nightmare Alley》是一张以电竖琴与原声竖琴为核心的实验性专辑，作品跨越自由爵士与电子声响的边界。整张专辑由十五首短小精悍的段落组成，从三分钟到七分钟不等，呈现出碎片化、即兴化的结构特征。Parkins 作为纽约地下实验场景的重要人物，作品融合了原声乐器的物理质感与电子处理的变形潜力，从抽象的音景雕塑到带有旋律碎片的小品皆有涉及。专辑由小众厂牌 Table of the Elements 于 1993 年发行，后于 2004 年以木质礼盒版重新发行，体现厂牌对实体收藏与艺术定位的重视。录音在 Baby Monster Studio 完成，由 Elliott Sharp 负责前期母带处理，整体制作保持了地下独立厂牌特有的粗糙质感与艺术纯粹性。
